content: Cefotetan, marketed under the brand name CEFOTAN, is a sterile, semisynthetic, broad-spectrum cephalosporin antibiotic belonging to the cephamycin subclass. It is resistant to beta-lactamase enzymes and is intended for parenteral administration. The active ingredient, cefotetan disodium, is the disodium salt of a complex chemical compound with the molecular formula C17H15N7Na2O8S4 and a molecular weight of 619.57. CEFOTAN is supplied as a white to pale yellow powder that is highly soluble in water. When reconstituted, the solution is suitable for intravenous (IV) or intramuscular (IM) administration. The appearance of the reconstituted solution ranges from colorless to yellow, depending on its concentration, and its pH typically falls between 4.5 and 6.5. For IV use, CEFOTAN in the ADD-Vantage Vial must be diluted with the appropriate volume of ADD-Vantage diluent solution. CEFOTAN is available in two vial strengths: Each 1 g vial contains cefotetan disodium equivalent to 1 g of cefotetan activity. Each 2 g vial contains cefotetan disodium equivalent to 2 g of cefotetan activity. Additionally, CEFOTAN is available as a premixed frozen solution in Galaxy® plastic containers (PL 2040). These containers hold a sterile, iso-osmotic, nonpyrogenic solution of cefotetan disodium, with either 1 g or 2 g of cefotetan activity in 50 mL of solution. Dextrose, USP, is added to adjust the osmolality to approximately 300 mOsmol/kg, with 1.9 g of dextrose in the 1 g dosage and 1.1 g in the 2 g dosage. Sodium bicarbonate is included to convert cefotetan free acid into its sodium salt form, and the pH is adjusted to a range of 4.0 to 6.5 using sodium bicarbonate and, if necessary, hydrochloric acid. Each gram of cefotetan activity in CEFOTAN contains 80 mg (3.5 mEq) of sodium. After thawing to room temperature, the premixed solution in the Galaxy® container is intended for IV use only. The Galaxy® container is made from a specially designed multilayer plastic (PL 2040), with the solution in contact with the polyethylene layer. While small amounts of certain chemical components from the plastic may leach into the solution over time, the safety of the container has been confirmed through animal testing in accordance with USP biological tests for plastic containers and tissue culture toxicity studies.
